propositions: Blocking edges written under the old ticket-type-tier rule are now wrong under the structural hierarchy rule and do not self-heal, distorting ready, next-batch, and the parent-first claim cascade.

A new read-only rebar link-audit command scans net-active blocking edges and classifies each via resolve_hierarchy_link as ancestor-blocking, mis-escalated, unreadable, or clean, with opt-in --repair.
Repair writes the replacement LINK before UNLINK so it is resumable and idempotent and never loses a dependency, and always fails safe by leaving the edge in place with repair_status unrepairable.
Ambiguous pairs (where the next UNLINK would cancel a different relation) are reported unrepairable and never repaired, since the event model has no relation-scoped unlink.
run_repair holding the tracker write lock across its loop is a self-deadlock defect; live repair was completed with an incremental per-write driver as a workaround, with the true fix deferred.
Mis-escalated edges whose resolved source is closed cannot be repaired because add_dependency refuses a link with a closed source, leaving inert residual findings between closed tickets.
